title: Sourcing and sinking I/O (PNP and NPN)
summary: Sinking inputs need a sensor that supplies +24 V (PNP); sourcing inputs need a sensor that switches to 0 V (NPN). A mismatch makes the input never switch.

sections.heading: Current direction
sections.body: The terms describe which side supplies current. A **sinking input** receives current: the sensor must connect the input to +24 V. A **PNP** (sourcing) sensor does exactly that. A **sourcing input** delivers current: the sensor must connect the input to 0 V, which an **NPN** (sinking) sensor does. Mechanical contacts work with both when wired accordingly.

sections.heading: Typical regional practice
sections.body: PNP sensors with sinking inputs dominate in Europe; NPN is common in parts of Asia. Many modules can be wired either way through a common terminal. Always check the module and the sensor data sheet.

sections.heading: Symptom of a mismatch
sections.body: The sensor's own LED switches, but the PLC input LED never does and the voltage at the input terminal does not change. In PLC Lab a PNP/NPN mismatch is a simulated fault: measure the input terminal to see it.
